42912647.text: Solitary ectopic insulinomas without concurrent pancreatic or gastrointestinal lesions are exceedingly rare. We report the 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT findings of a solitary ectopic insulinoma in a 68-year-old woman with a 10-year history of recurrent hypoglycemic syncope. Endogenous hyperinsulinemia was confirmed, but conventional imaging and laparoscopic pancreatic exploration were negative. PET/CT revealed a solitary intense focus in the para-abdominal aortic region. Surgical resection confirmed a solitary ectopic insulinoma, and postoperative hypoglycemia resolved. This case highlights the value of 18 F-NOTA-exendin-4 PET/CT in identifying occult solitary ectopic insulinomas when conventional imaging and surgical exploration are unrevealing, enabling curative resection.

42955597.label: Objectives
42955597.text: To develop and validate a deep learning (DL)-based CT model integrating pancreatic imaging and CT-derived body composition for severity prediction in acute pancreatitis (AP).

42955597.label: Materials and methods
42955597.text: In this retrospective dual-center study, patients with AP who underwent CT within 72 h of symptom onset were enrolled from January 2021 to September 2025 at Center 1 and January 2023 to September 2024 at Center 2. The primary dataset (n = 426) was randomly divided into a training set (n = 298) and an internal test set (n = 128), while 110 patients from Center 2 served as the external test set. A three-dimensional DL model was developed for pancreatic imaging, and two-dimensional DL models were constructed for L3-level visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and skeletal muscle (SM). Six predictive models were constructed: clinical, pancreas, VAT, SM, pancreas-clinical (PC), and combined. Performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, DeLong testing, calibration, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).

42955597.label: Results
42955597.text: The combined model achieved area under the curve (AUCs) of 0.897 (95% CI: 0.862-0.932), 0.909 (95% CI: 0.861-0.958), and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.856-0.964) in the training, internal test, and external test sets, respectively. The combined model outperformed the PC model in the training set (p = 0.002) and external test set (p = 0.020). NRI and IDI analyses confirmed the incremental predictive value of body composition features.

42955597.label: Conclusions
42955597.text: A CT-based DL model integrating pancreatic imaging, body composition, and clinical variables demonstrated good performance for AP severity prediction.

42955597.label: Key points
42955597.text: Question Early severity stratification in AP remains challenging because conventional clinical and imaging assessments may not fully capture pancreatic injury and systemic disease status. Findings A CT-based DL model integrating pancreatic imaging, body composition, and clinical variables demonstrated good performance for severity prediction in AP. Critical Relevance Statement This study evaluates the value of integrating pancreatic imaging and CT-derived body composition information and supports the use of routinely acquired CT data for early risk stratification, potentially facilitating more individualized monitoring and management of AP.

42957197.text: For decades, low gallbladder ejection fraction (GBEF), measured with hepatobiliary scintigraphy after infusion of sincalide, has been used to diagnose symptomatic biliary hypokinesia and as a predictor of the necessity for cholecystectomy. Recently, gallbladder hypercontractility (GBEF > 79%) has been recognized as a cause of right upper quadrant pain, and cholecystectomy has often resulted in symptom relief. This retrospective study evaluated follow-up data collected after GBEF studies to determine the incidence of cholecystectomy or persistence of symptoms. Methods: We evaluated all GBEF biliary studies performed at our institution between January 1, 2012, and December 31, 2025. Study reports containing "ejection fraction" and "sincalide" were identified to establish the study population. All patients presented with right upper quadrant pain. They received 185 MBq (range, 111-259 MBq) of 99mTc-mebrofenin intravenously and were imaged in a 20° left anterior oblique position for 60 min. Once the gallbladder was clearly seen, the patients were given a 30-min intravenous infusion of sincalide (0.02 μg/kg), and imaging was continued for a total of 45 min. Patients were categorized as having probable gallbladder disease (cholecystectomy and resolution of symptoms or no cholecystectomy and persistent symptoms) or unlikely gallbladder disease (cholecystectomy and persistent symptoms or no cholecystectomy and resolved symptoms or other diagnosis). Results: In total, 1775 patients were included in the final analysis. Forty percent of patients had a GBEF of greater than 79%, and 27% had a GBEF of less than 39%. Of those who underwent cholecystectomy, 90% of those with a GBEF of less than 39% and 94% of those with a GBEF of greater than 79% experienced symptom relief. The incidence of probable biliary disease was 61% in patients with a low GBEF and 44% in patients with a high GBEF and was lowest in the group with a GBEF of 60%-69% (24% of patients). Conclusion: Our study found that hepatobiliary GBEF is not as accurate as we have assumed. Additional clinical criteria are needed to improve patient selection and positive outcomes. The high percentage of patients with a GBEF exceeding 79% has not been appreciated, as most of the previous studies evaluated healthy subjects and did not examine outcomes. These results should shift how we think about GBEF studies and how the results are reported.

42977647.label: Aims
42977647.text: The incremental diagnostic value of artificial intelligence (AI) in coronary CT angiography (CCTA) remains uncertain. We compared five CCTA strategies: automated stenosis assessment software (COR Analyzer), stand-alone CCTA-based deep learning (DL), junior readers, senior readers, and AI-assisted readers, for detecting anatomical coronary artery stenosis against invasive coronary angiography.

42977647.label: Methods and results
42977647.text: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through July 9, 2026. Twenty-two observational diagnostic accuracy studies were included (19 retrospective and three prospective; 21 for ≥50% stenosis and six for ≥70% stenosis). In the primary patient-level analysis at ≥50% stenosis, pooled sensitivity for DL and AI-assisted readers was 0.91 each (95% credible interval, 0.87 to 0.94 and 0.86 to 0.94), versus 0.80 (0.73-0.87) for junior and 0.87 (0.82-0.91) for senior readers; AI assistance increased sensitivity by 0.10 versus junior readers (0.06-0.15) and 0.03 versus senior readers (0.01-0.06). Specificity was similar across DL and reader strategies (0.64-0.67) but markedly lower for COR Analyzer (0.25 [0.15 to 0.38]). In the smaller ≥70% network, AI-assisted reading showed the highest estimated sensitivity (0.80 [0.70 to 0.88]). Findings were robust to outlier exclusion; certainty was low to very low for most ≥50% outcomes.

42977647.label: Conclusion
42977647.text: Stand-alone DL and AI-assisted reading had similar estimated diagnostic performance. AI assistance improved sensitivity most clearly for less-experienced readers. These accuracy comparisons did not establish formal equivalence or determine whether stand-alone DL could replace human interpretation in clinical practice.

42984197.label: Objective
42984197.text: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.

42984197.label: Materials and methods
42984197.text: A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.

42984197.label: Results
42984197.text: Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.

42984197.label: Conclusion
42984197.text: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

43002597.text: A 39-year-old man suffering from Graves' ophthalmopathy, which was resistant to steroids (with a clinical activity score of 5/7 and a moderate-severe EUGOGO grade), had a 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan. This scan showed strong bilateral FAPI activity in the extraocular muscles, especially in the inferior recti, even though his visual acuity remained normal. A later low-dose 177Lu-FAPI-2286 retention study confirmed that the radiotracer stayed selectively within the recti. This example suggests that fibroblast activation protein-targeted theranostics could be a new way to image and possibly treat Graves' orbitopathy.
